project.name: Salmond's Muir
project.boundarySource: Mapped named-place location with a conservative editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Full strict-boundary audit completed. The local HES statutory and NRHE imports returned zero records. Four dated Angus HER records are retained from a current cultural-heritage gazetteer, without presenting them as attractions. Current OSM and named-provider searches found no qualifying See, Eat, dedicated trail, picnic site, public car park or public toilet. The Carnoustie path-network road link is context only and its own warning says it is not recommended for walkers or unaccompanied children. Angus-wide full audit completed 2026-09-01: all six visitor categories, the four named commercial trail providers, current official/conventional routes, strict-boundary scoring and local HES/NRHE integrity were checked.

touristAppeal.label: Minor Interest
touristAppeal.summary: A very small A92-edge hamlet with documentary and archaeological history but no independently visitable centre, attraction or visitor-service cluster. Nearby East Haven, Panbride and Carnoustie are not transferred into its score.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The road-edge setting and agricultural surroundings offer no verified destination-scale dog visit; use only mapped rights of way and keep dogs under close control.

townGuide.headline: A regional reference rather than a visitor stop
townGuide.intro: Salmond's Muir scores 28% and remains in the Angus selector but off the main town map. Its history is retained in the heat layer, while neighbouring coast and town facilities remain assigned to their own places.
perfectFor: Recognising the historic place-name while travelling between Carnoustie and Arbroath
townGuide.visitorMood: A small roadside hamlet whose interest is documentary rather than a public visitor experience.
